notes.title: Organ Quarter Update 1.2.00
notes.content:
[h1]Hello![/h1]

It has been some time. 
We hope you have been well...

[b]This major update - version 1.2.00 - is now available.[/b]

This major update adds new supported languages, achievements, improves support for many VR headsets, and much more:

[list]
[*] Subtitles for: Korean, Chinese (Traditional) and (Simplified), German, Spanish (Mexico), French (France), English, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil)
[*] Achievements
[*] Support for QUEST headset and controllers
[*] Major performance optimizations
[*] Reworking of collisions and general comfort
[*] Fixing of several game-breaking bugs
[*] Other minor tweaks/fixes
[/list]

Thanks again for your support and watch this space for future updates!

Best,
The Outer Brain Team

notes.title: Organ Quarter patch 1.04 now live (Windows MR support + more)
notes.content:
[b]Hello![/b]

Thanks for the amazing support, helping us reach [b]98% positive reviews on Steam![/b]

The third patch for Organ Quarter - version 1.04 - is now available.
 
[h1]Improvements in this patch include:[/h1]
[list]
    [*]early Windows MR support (only trackpad movement supported for now)
    [*]a new “current ammo” counter
    [*]click-in only movement option
    [*]smooth rotation option
    [*]a couple of new secrets in the game world
    [*]minor props added to several scenes
    [*]fixed a bug where player’s couldn’t properly defeat a mid-game monster
    [*]other minor tweaks and bug fixes
[/list]

Thanks again for your support and watch this space for future updates!

Best,
The Outer Brain Team

notes.title: First Organ Quarter patch now live! 1.02
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

The first patch for Organ Quarter is now live. Thank you to everyone who has bought the game and supported us thus far. You guys have been so awesome.

[h1]Here are some of the improvements included with this patch:[/h1] 


[list]
    [*]fixed/overhauled the left hand control options for both HTC Vive and Oculus Touch controllers
    [*]fixed and refined teleport locomotion (fewer teleportation blockages and better responsiveness)
    [*]fixed the vignette slider for added comfort during analog locomotion
    [*]vastly improved performance throughout the experience
    [*]added an anti-aliasing slider so players can select their ideal level of anti-aliasing in-game
    [*]added the ability for the gun hand to grab objects from inventory
    [*]other minor tweaks/fixes
[/list]

Let us know how you find the improvements and please comment here or in the Forums if you experience any issues. 

[b]Next on our list we will be tackling the map saving bug.[/b] Thank you, everyone, for your patience!

With love,
The Outer Brain Team

[*]fixed and refined teleport locomotion (fewer teleportation blockages and better responsiveness)
[*]fixed the vignette slider for added comfort during analog locomotion
[*]other minor tweaks/fixes
[b]Next on our list we will be tackling the map saving bug.[/b]

notes.title: Organ Quarter post-release roadmap
notes.content:
[b]Thank you to everyone who has bought Organ Quarter and supported us throughout development! [/b]

Today we share our plans for the game moving forward. This is a simple road map of several months’ FREE content updates and quality of life improvements.

The updates to follow in coming days, weeks and months will include:
[olist]
    [*]Multiple hotfixes and bug fixes 
    [*]The Organ Quarter Soundtrack as optional DLC (on Steam and Bandcamp) 
    [*]A substantial Quality of Life update (better menus and options, more detail in environments, more control options and gameplay options)
[*]The Non-VR Update (which will provide non-VR players with a monitor-friendly build for the game)
[/olist]

[h1] #1 Multiple hotfixes and bugfixes [/h1]

These smaller updates will be rolled out consistently as we gather reports from you (the players) prioritise the most serious issues and address them. 

We are already aware of several minor issues in the game which will be addressed ASAP. Our highest priorities are:
[olist]
    [*]The ‘Left handed’ control option for Oculus Touch users doesn’t work
    [*]When you enter and leave a TV, the stamps on your map often will be erased
    [*](Minor location spoilers from halfway through the game:) Once you insert a battery into the large battery-powered gates in the Mines, they will change state whenever you re-enter the room. Meaning if you insert a battery the gate will open, but then if you leave the room and re-enter, the gate will close. To fix this you can simply leave the room and re-enter
[/olist]

[h1] #2 The Organ Quarter Soundtrack [/h1]

We are incredibly proud of Anadale’s work on the Organ Quarter soundtrack so will be releasing the 40+ track soundtrack as paid DLC for Organ Quarter and separately on Bandcamp.com. 

[h1] #3 The Quality of Life update [/h1]

This substantial update will be released between now and Christmas. We are targetting 31 November. Our current plans for the QoL update include:

[list]
    [*]New optional environments and secrets
    [*]Improved environments throughout: better textures, better lighting, better blending, more miscellaneous objects 
    [*]Improved VR interactions throughout: interactive appliances, furniture, miscellaneous objects 
    [*]New control options (click-in movement for Vive, among others)
    [*]The ability to scroll through previously used/collected maps
    [*]The ability to look at previously seen side texts
[/list]

These are liable to change and other unannounced improvements may be included.


[h1]#4 The Non-VR Update[/h1]

Depending on complexity of task, this will follow between December 2017 and February 2018.

This will be a build of Organ Quarter which functions on a normal monitor without a VR HMD system.

This will be a drastically different experience from the current (ground-up VR) version. Controls, interfaces, puzzles, enemies and level designs are likely to change to account for the lack of hand-tracked controllers. 

Stay tuned for more news,
Outer Brain Team
